For the Pairwise Q-distribution, the autoregressive conditional is constructed as the geometric mean of the pairwise class-conditional distributions between the new feature and each previously selected feature:

\[
q(x_{f_t}\mid x_{f_{<t}},y)
=
\left(\prod_{i=1}^{t-1} p(x_{f_t}\mid x_{f_i},y)\right)^{1/(t-1)}.
\]

This makes the model more general than the Naive Bayes Q-distribution while remaining tractable, since the full \(q(x_S\mid y)\) can be computed from tractable autoregressive conditionals [6][7]. The authors also justify it computationally by showing that the resulting conditionals can be updated recursively when a new feature is selected:

\[
q(x_i\mid x_{S_t},y)
=
\left[p(x_i\mid x_{f_t},y)\,
q(x_i\mid x_{S_{t-1}},y)^{t-1}\right]^{1/t},
\]

so the algorithm need not recompute them from scratch [5].

VMR_mRMR preserves the following state across iterations:

- The entropy score of each feature, stored by feature ID after the initial parallel map computation [4].
- Each feature’s relevance score with respect to the decision variable \(d_t\), since this score does not depend on the selected subset and therefore need not be recomputed [6].
- The selected-feature subset \(s_F\), including the most recently selected feature, which is broadcast for the next calculation [2][7].

Consequently, each iteration does not recompute relevance or all feature-pair redundancies. It computes the conditional-entropy terms for the remaining candidates \(F-s_F\): relative to \(d_t\) in the first iteration, and relative to only the most recently selected feature in subsequent iterations [8]. These values are then used to form the incremental mRMR scores [3].
question_answers.fetch-032:
VMR_mRMR uses a **memorized map/data structure of the relevant attribute-value pairs—`possiblePairs`—and their frequencies**. These values can then be retrieved to calculate conditional entropy; the map also enables constant-time item retrieval. [5] [7]

It avoids contingency tables and histograms because constructing them is computationally intensive and consumes more space, proportional to the product of the feature-domain sizes. Instead, VMR_mRMR computes only the needed entropy and conditional-entropy values and restricts pair calculations to `possiblePairs`, avoiding redundant work. [8]

\[
\sqrt{\frac{n}{p_n s_n^2\log(p_n)}}\,\lambda_n\to\infty,
\]
under the theorem’s other assumptions; then the estimator sets the true zero coefficients to zero with probability tending to one [5].

\[

whereas Theorem 3.6 requires \(\lambda_n\) to be asymptotically larger, on the order of \(\sqrt{p_n}\) times that scale. Thus, when \(p_n\) grows, the LASSO’s consistency requirement is incompatible with the stronger tuning condition needed for the stated sparsistency theorem [8].

question_answers.operator-001:
Filter methods select variables during preprocessing, using their intrinsic relevance or predictive strength—often by ranking variables and applying a threshold—before the forecasting model is run. They are independent of the learning method, making them efficient and generally better at generalization [2][4][7][8].

Wrapper methods, by contrast, wrap the variable-selection process around a forecasting or learning method. They use the model’s predictive performance as the objective and search—often heuristically—for the subset that yields the best forecasting performance, so they are dependent on the chosen model [5][6][8].
